config.title: Infinite Scroll

intro.title: Infinite Scroll
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue app that implements an infinite scroll feature, allowing users to continuously load more items as they scroll down a list. You will learn the core concept of detecting scroll position and triggering data fetching when the user reaches the bottom of the page. The main technologies involved include Vue's reactive state, lifecycle hooks, and event listeners for scroll events. By the end, you'll have a functional component that dynamically loads and displays data, enhancing user experience with seamless content loading.
intro.usecase: Infinite scroll is a fundamental pattern in modern web applications where content loads progressively as users scroll down, creating a seamless browsing experience. You'll implement this in social media feeds like Facebook or Twitter, e-commerce product listings on Amazon, and content-heavy platforms like YouTube or news aggregators. As a Vue developer, you'll use this technique to build efficient dashboards that display large datasets without overwhelming initial load times, or in admin panels where users need to browse through extensive records. Mastering infinite scroll helps you create applications that feel responsive while managing performance and data fetching intelligently.

objectives: Initialize a Vue component with reactive state for managing scrollable data
Implement a scroll event handler to detect when users reach the bottom of a page
Construct an API data fetching method that integrates with Vue's lifecycle hooks
Configure conditional rendering to display loading indicators during data retrieval
Manipulate arrays in Vue's reactive system to append new items to existing lists
Apply computed properties to control when infinite scroll triggers should activate
Bind scroll event listeners to DOM elements using Vue template directives

steps.title: Wire scroll handler to window scroll event
steps.instruction: Add an event listener for the 'scroll' event on the window object that calls your scroll detection handler, and also add the cleanup to remove it when the component unmounts.
steps.hint: Use window.addEventListener('scroll', handler) inside onMounted, and window.removeEventListener('scroll', handler) in onUnmounted.
steps.expectedOutcome: The scroll handler will be triggered when the user scrolls, and the event listener will be properly cleaned up when the component is destroyed.
successCriteria: The window scroll event listener is added in onMounted, calls the scroll detection handler, and is removed in onUnmounted.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
